subject: sociology
title: Representation Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: How does the media picture gender, ethnicity, age and class? Stretch into exam-grade evaluation.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam stretch on media representation of gender, ethnicity, age and class.
final_note: Always evaluate: name the stereotype, give a current example, suggest if it is changing.

concepts.def: How the media portrays a group or idea.
A fixed, simplified image of a group.
Mulvey: women shown from a heterosexual male view.
Groups missing or trivialised in media.
Cohen: groups blamed during moral panics.
Choosing news that fits owners' values.

walkthroughs.body_html: Liberal feminists note more female leads but still in 'domestic' or sexualised roles. Mulvey's male gaze idea argues camera angles still treat women as objects. Recent shows like I May Destroy You challenge this.

Studies show ethnic minorities over-represented as criminals or athletes and under-represented as experts. Young people are often portrayed as 'folk devils', while older people face symbolic annihilation — invisible in advertising.
Define representation. Give one classic study (e.g., Mulvey). Give a current example (a named show or app). Offer a counter (changing representations, audience choice). Conclude with judgement.
